hit.pose: early impact onset, same protective bent elbows as corrected master, both feet planted

Force from screen-right pushes shoulders and head LEFT/back about 25 source pixels relative to hips by spinal articulation. Flex both knees more, chest now clearly E-side. Eyes squeezed, chin draws back. Keep shoes planted pointing right, no full-image translation. Right elbow raises the lantern grip near ribs protectively; left flask stays at sternum. Hair trails slightly to screen-right relative to recoiling head, showing force direction.

Maximum but controlled EAST-hit recoil: torso leans backward toward screen-left about 12 degrees from upright while hips sink through bent knees; head slightly farther LEFT/back than frame02. Front/rightmost shoe remains planted with shin resisting force, rear shoe also bears weight; no airborne foot. Near right hand guards at ribs and lantern tilts gently with inertia; left jade flask firmly held to chest. Clearly the reaction peak, not attack and not falling.

The backward reaction has stopped and rebound begins. Bring chest halfway from recoil peak toward upright, knees still compressed, head recovering toward EAST. Both shoes planted in the same standing locations, neither toe turns toward camera. The right lantern arm lowers slightly from guard while the far left bottle remains protected. Expression still strained but one eye starts opening. Hair and tassels continue a small delayed backward wave.

Recovery after impact: torso nearly upright and weight centered between the same planted feet, knees extend partway. Eyes now open looking EAST, mouth relaxed from wince. Right elbow opens a little to lower lantern beside right ribs; left bottle settles lower toward chest/upper abdomen. Distinct from master impact: shoulders no longer recoil and face no longer tightly winces.

End of hit recovery, balanced quiet EAST guard. Torso upright, softly unlocked knees and both right-pointing shoes planted. Calm alert face, no wince. Right hand holds lantern slightly forward of right hip with elbow naturally bent, left bottle close to torso. Hair and sleeves largely settled. New independent final drawing, not copied/reused frame01; this is recovered guard, not another impact.

attack.pose: corrected initial lantern backswing, stable support

Early weight loading. Compared with master01 lower pelvis through knee flexion about 12 source pixels, compact stable fore/aft stance. Near RIGHT shoulder draws backward slightly and elbow remains bent, lantern hand close behind right ribs; lantern body hangs behind hip. LEFT bottle stays protected near chest. Face EAST, no camera turn. Both shoe long axes point RIGHT, no front-facing rear shoe.

Maximum compact anticipation before the swing: chest winds backward only slightly in EAST side plane; near RIGHT upper arm behind ribs and elbow flexed, grip drawn close to rear waist. Hanging lantern bowl swings backward/up a little but remains whole inside canvas. Knees compressed, weight on rear support. LEFT jade flask protected at chest. Keep the existing head scale, no turn toward viewer, feet planted RIGHTward.

Begin forward shoulder/elbow-driven lantern attack. Push through rear foot, pelvis shifts EAST slightly by posture while both feet remain planted. Near RIGHT elbow passes beside ribs from behind to a middle position; hand/lantern pass next to hip, not behind extreme and not fully forward yet. LEFT bottle held stable against upper torso. Readable upper-arm then forearm action, no staff or magical projectile.

Forward swing acceleration: near RIGHT shoulder rotates forward in EAST plane and bent elbow moves ahead of ribs; right grip now ahead of abdomen, hanging lotus lantern has crossed from rear to front at waist/chest height. Elbow partly opening, not fully locked. Body leans EAST about 4 degrees, front leg accepts weight, both shoes planted along RIGHTward axis. LEFT bottle tucked close on far side. Keep full lamp inside x<1210, not enlarged.

The clear active contact moment of a short lantern swing toward EAST. Near RIGHT shoulder and elbow push the short curved handle forward, elbow almost extended but still bent enough to keep full lantern within canvas. Lantern bowl is clearly in FRONT of torso and slightly below hand, near x1080,y770 (approximate, do not change global framing), never a long staff. Front knee braces, rear leg drives, both right-facing shoes still grounded. LEFT jade flask protected at chest. Determined expression. No enemy, no hit spark or baked projectile: only the physical attack pose.

Immediately after contact, a short controlled follow-through. Right arm continues a little forward/down relative to contact, large lantern bowl drops slightly through a forward arc without touching floor or being clipped. Torso leans forward briefly while front knee absorbs movement, rear heel may lift a little but rear toes stay planted pointing RIGHT. LEFT bottle remains near chest. A readable physical follow-through distinct from the anticipation master.

Brake the forward lantern swing. Near RIGHT elbow begins flexing from extended contact back toward torso, lantern still in front but no longer at maximum reach; shoulder drops slightly. Front knee compresses under momentum, rear heel returns down. Both feet retain RIGHTward long axes and original standing support region. Far left bottle held firmly, no mirrored hands, no screen-front shoe.

Retract after strike: near RIGHT forearm folds toward lower ribs, grip passing toward front of hip, lantern hangs in front-side at waist height. Torso returns from forward lean toward neutral and weight recenters over planted feet. LEFT bottle at chest. No attack at full reach now; calm determined face, hair/sleeves slightly delayed.

Late recovery: upright E-facing body, knees partly straighten. Near RIGHT elbow returns beside ribs, lamp grip lowered to hip-level at body side; lantern now alongside hip, not far behind or forward extreme. LEFT bottle settles close upper abdomen. Two shoes planted RIGHTward in compact fore/aft stance. Preserve hairstyle and all original props.

Almost ready after attack. Near RIGHT shoulder relaxed with elbow softly bent holding the lantern at right side slightly forward; lantern swing nearly stopped. Left hand keeps jade bottle close torso. Torso upright, knees softly unlocked, eyes focused EAST. Both right-pointing feet stable. This must be distinct from frame10 by further settling of shoulder, lamp and sleeves, not a duplicate.

End of attack recovery, settled EAST combat guard. Near right hand holds short lantern handle beside right ribs/hip; hanging lamp rests clear of leg; far left jade flask held safely at chest. Balanced planted right-pointing shoes, no outward splay. Alert neutral face, no recoil or running pose. Independently draw a final guard close to readiness, not a reused/copy of frame01 and not maximum backswing.

cast.pose: corrected initial gathering, lantern in front and bottle at chest

Begin gathering: far LEFT elbow flexes to lift the jade flask slightly higher toward sternum; near RIGHT elbow also flexes to bring the lantern grip 15 pixels inward toward right ribs. Lantern remains suspended in front, not behind. Knees softly flex, torso upright facing EAST. Both shoes planted and point RIGHT. Calm concentration, no visible energy effects.

Gathering deepens: both elbows closer to torso, far-left jade bottle raised near upper chest with neck upright, near-right lantern handle slightly higher near chest. The large lotus lamp bowl hangs ahead of abdomen, clear of knees. Chin dips a little, gaze toward EAST/bottle area, knees flex slightly more. No crossed or switched hands, no movement of world root.

Concentrated gathering peak: head/chin lower slightly and eyes focus with relaxed narrowed lids. Both props drawn slightly nearer chest, right elbow deeply flexed, left jade flask tucked just below sternum. Knees bend to store motion without shifting feet, torso still E side profile. Lamp retains original size and contains only its normal light; no aura/circle/particles.

Begin channeling from gathered pose: near RIGHT shoulder starts lifting/opening forward, hand raises the lotus handle slightly above previous level; lamp rises toward upper abdomen/chest, still comfortably below face. Far LEFT jade flask remains close sternum. Torso lengthens from slight compression while feet stay planted. Show a clear change in elbow angle, not a duplicate still.

Continue deliberate lamp lift: near RIGHT elbow moves forward of ribs, hand at lower chest level; the upright hanging lotus lamp sits farther forward and a little higher. Far LEFT hand maintains bottle close chest, neck upright. Body stays EAST, both shoes point right and remain planted. Keep full lamp within right canvas edge and do not cover face.

Final pre-release preparation. Near right shoulder holds raised lantern grip forward with elbow partly flexed, left bottle drawn near sternum and rotated only slightly outward while held securely. Knees softly bend and body leans EAST about 2 degrees; face focused. This is anticipation of release, not release at full reach. No magic trails or baked effects.

Release begins: near RIGHT elbow extends a small deliberate amount toward EAST, lantern moves ahead of torso; far LEFT bottle hand also begins a smaller forward motion near chest without crossing right arm. Torso rises from preparation and shifts weight through legs, planted feet unchanged. Eyes open with intent. Keep lamp upright and its full outline safely inside canvas.

The main casting release keyframe. Near RIGHT shoulder/elbow extends lantern forward toward EAST, almost at comfortable reach; far LEFT hand presents the jade bottle just forward of sternum, still behind the lantern and firmly held. Torso leans EAST about 3 degrees over stable planted legs. The hanging lamp remains a curved short handle and large lotus bowl, no staff. Clearly open arm silhouette at release compared with gathering; no beams, projectiles, circles, runes or broad glow.

A short continuing release after the peak, independently drawn: right elbow relaxes a few degrees while hand remains forward, lamp drops slightly through a small natural pendulum motion; left bottle held forward near sternum. Torso starts returning toward upright. Face still focused EAST. Feet planted, no identical copy of release09, no new effects.

Release tails off: near RIGHT shoulder lowers and elbow begins folding, lantern still in front of torso but drawn slightly inward/down from release. Far LEFT hand begins withdrawing flask toward chest. Knees relax and body returns upright. A physical arm recovery, no residual spell particles.

Both original prop hands retract. Near RIGHT elbow folds toward ribs and lowers handle, bringing lamp toward front of waist; far LEFT elbow bends to return bottle securely near chest. Torso upright in EAST side view, knees softly unlocked, feet fixed pointing RIGHT. Face concentrating but relaxed.

Late casting recovery: right lantern hand near right lower ribs with lantern hanging at waist ahead of hip; left jade bottle close torso upper abdomen. Shoulders drop slightly. Hair/sleeves/tassels show modest lag then settle. Feet maintain same E-facing support, no turn toward viewer.

Settle shoulders and elbows further after casting: right hand lowers lamp handle a little, elbow relaxed but bent; left bottle rests comfortably at chest/upper abdomen. Head returns to normal alert EAST gaze, no lowered concentrating chin. Upright balanced body, both toes pointing RIGHT. No running movement.

Almost settled EAST guard after cast. Right lantern hand relaxed beside front of hip, lantern vertical with only tiny remaining sway, far left bottle protected against torso. Knees almost straight but unlocked. Sleeves and long wavy hair mostly still. Distinct independent frame from14 through smaller lowered hand position and settled cloth.

Final settled EAST casting guard. Calm focused gaze, upright torso, stable planted RIGHTward shoes. Near anatomical RIGHT arm naturally bent with lotus lantern at front-right waist; far LEFT hand holds jade flask at chest. Motion finished, no release extension or magical effects. Draw a new final frame rather than copying initial master; retain global scale, camera and root.
